question: Can a sparsity-regularized equation-learning network predict nanocrystal size competitively while exposing compact, chemically meaningful mechanisms for product, precursor, and process effects?

key_findings.claim: NanoEQL closes much of the predictive gap between symbolic white-box models and black-box tree ensembles on the nanocrystal dataset.
key_findings.evidence: On the held-out test set, NanoEQL reaches R-squared 0.65 and mean absolute percentage error 0.35, versus R-squared 0.27 for PySR; random forest reaches R-squared 0.64 and MAPE 0.32. Errors are larger above about 25 nm.

key_findings.claim: Smoothing singular symbolic operators improves both optimization stability and predictive accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: The model replaces reciprocal, square-root, and cube-root operators near zero with smooth forms; for the reciprocal ablation, this prevents pathological overuse and raises test R-squared from 0.54 to 0.65.

anchors.section: EQL Architecture Based on Gated Attention

key_findings.claim: The fitted top-level relationship is a sparse linear combination of three interpretable latent scalars.
key_findings.evidence: The final equation is size = 5.344 Zrea + 2.245(-Zops) + 2.53(-Zp) + 14.97. Product, precursor-reaction, and operation branches are pruned into equations over original descriptors; performance plateaus near 60% pruning while expression complexity grows rapidly below that sparsity.

key_findings.claim: The temperature gate learns different concentration-versus-reactivity regimes for inorganic and organic precursors.
key_findings.evidence: The mean learned reactivity coefficient is 0.18 for inorganic precursors and 0.33 for organic precursors. Inorganic behavior becomes reactivity driven mainly above 300 degrees Celsius, while organic concentration dominance appears mainly at very short reaction time.

anchors.section: Physical Significance of the Three Scalars and Synthesis Mechanisms

key_findings.claim: A PbSe intervention qualitatively validates the model's precursor-ratio mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: The learned reaction space predicts that increasing selenium content lowers Zrea and nanocrystal size. Holding other conditions fixed experimentally, changing Pb:Se from 1:0.25 to 1:4 reduces average particle size from 9.5 nm to 6.1 nm.

anchors.section: Physical Significance of the Three Scalars and Synthesis Mechanisms

key_findings.claim: The architecture transfers to a distinct organic reaction-yield task without losing most black-box accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: On the Buchwald-Hartwig cross-coupling dataset, NanoEQL reports R-squared 0.93 and mean absolute error 4.89%, exceeding random forest and XGBoost and approaching LightGBM at R-squared 0.94.

method.core_idea: Build chemical process structure into an equation-learning network so that product properties, process conditions, and permutation-invariant precursor interactions reduce to sparse symbolic scalars before a linear final prediction.
method.mechanism: Featurize products and inorganic precursors with matminer and organics with RDKit, remove collinear descriptors using VIF, pass each branch through an EQL library of eight symbolic operators, and pool precursor embeddings with seven statistics. A process-conditioned softmax gate mixes molar-fraction and learned-reactivity weights. Optimize Smooth L1 loss plus L1 sparsity on symbolic layers, tune with nested cross-validation and Optuna, prune the trained graph, and read the surviving equations and gates as candidate mechanisms.
assumptions: The curated synthesis recipes and descriptors cover the chemistry needed for the held-out compounds and conditions.
The chosen operator library can express relevant empirical mechanisms compactly.
Sparse predictive equations and gated weights correspond to chemically meaningful factors rather than dataset shortcuts.
Molar concentration and a learned reactivity score are adequate top-level explanations of precursor importance.
A stratified random 15% test split is sufficient to judge generalization despite potential recipe, composition, or literature-source dependence.

techniques.role: Bounds gradients near zero for reciprocal and root functions while retaining their asymptotic symbolic behavior.
Mixes concentration-derived and learned-reactivity precursor weights as a function of injection temperature, reaction temperature, and time.
Aggregates variable precursor sets with weighted sum, mean, range, deviation, norm, maximum, and minimum without sequence dependence.
Maps product, operations, inorganic precursors, organic precursors, and their reactions into separately inspectable sparse expressions.
Uses L1 regularization and post-training pruning to trade predictive fit for equation compactness.
Varies Pb:Se ratio experimentally to test one qualitative prediction from the learned reaction scalar.

evaluations.setting: Nanocrystal synthesis dataset from the authors' prior work, 15% stratified held-out test split
evaluations.metric: R-squared and mean absolute percentage error for size
evaluations.baseline: PySR 0.27 R-squared; random forest 0.64 R-squared and 0.32 MAPE

evaluations.result: Smoothed reciprocal raises R-squared from 0.54 to 0.65 and reduces pathological singular-operator use
evaluations.baseline: Original reciprocal with clamping or shifting
Reported as better than random forest and XGBoost and near LightGBM at 0.94 R-squared

evaluations.setting: PbSe synthesis with all conditions fixed except selenium amount
evaluations.result: Mean size falls from 9.5 nm at Pb:Se 1:0.25 to 6.1 nm at 1:4
evaluations.baseline: Model-predicted direction of Zrea and size change

evaluations.result: 6,800 direct-gap semiconductors and 34,000 metallic materials ranked; known MoTe2, InP, and ZnSe nanocrystals receive low scores
evaluations.baseline: Qualitative agreement with selected known nanocrystal examples, without prospective synthesis-rate metrics

limitations: Reviewer-identified: the paper does not report dataset size, composition-group leakage checks, repeated split variance, or scaffold/out-of-distribution tests in the main text, so random-split generalization may be optimistic.
Reviewer-identified: named latent scalars are post hoc interpretations of predictive factors; sparsity and a plausible sign do not establish that the equations are causal mechanisms.

Reviewer-identified: only one qualitative PbSe precursor-ratio intervention is performed, with no replicate count, uncertainty bars, or direct comparison between predicted and measured sizes across all four ratios in text.
Reviewer-identified: screening validation is retrospective and selective; no high-ranked previously unknown material is synthesized to test -Zp prospectively.
Reviewer-identified: the top-level linear equation is reported from one fitted model without coefficient uncertainty or stability across folds and seeds.
Reviewer-identified: the attention gate uses an MLP reactivity scorer, so the overall system is not fully white-box at every intermediate operation despite symbolic branch outputs.
Reviewer-identified: MAPE is scale sensitive and the paper acknowledges larger errors for particles above 25 nm, where the training distribution and measurement noise may differ.
failure_modes: Symbolic branches can select correlated proxy descriptors even after VIF filtering, yielding chemically plausible but noncausal equations.
A smoothed singular operator may improve optimization while changing the physical law around zero in a data-dependent way.
The gate can collapse toward concentration or reactivity because its parameters receive a separate, tenfold-scale learning rate and are not L1 regularized.
Random recipe splits can leak nearly identical compositions or protocols across train and test.
Extreme pruning can produce a compact but unstable equation; weak pruning makes expressions combinatorially large and uninterpretable.
Materials outside the descriptor and reaction-condition support can receive confident -Zp rankings with no synthetic feasibility.
The model underpredicts or becomes unreliable for large nanocrystals, where measurement uncertainty and sparsity increase.
reusable_insights: Embed known permutation invariance and process structure before symbolic regression rather than asking a flat equation search to discover them.
Smooth singular operators at problematic feature values and audit both usage frequency and predictive effect.
Use branch-specific latent equations when different physical factors should remain separately inspectable.
Treat pruning ratio as a Pareto choice between error and equation complexity, not as a cosmetic post-processing step.
Convert an interpreted equation into a controlled intervention before calling it a mechanism.
Report the stability of discovered expressions across folds and seeds, not only the best predictive model.
open_questions: Do the three scalar equations and their coefficients remain stable across retraining seeds, literature sources, and composition-held-out splits?
Can prospective synthesis of high-ranked but unreported -Zp materials validate nanocrystallization capability?
How does NanoEQL compare with modern symbolic-regression systems under matched complexity and search budgets?
Can the MLP reactivity scorer itself be replaced by a sparse symbolic or mechanistic kinetics model?
Do predicted precursor interventions remain correct outside PbSe and across nucleation, growth, and postgrowth stages?
How should predictive and expression uncertainty propagate into materials rankings and experimental design?

competitive_landscape.title: Extrapolation and learning equations
competitive_landscape.difference: Martius and Lampert introduce the differentiable sparse Equation Learner that recovers analytical expressions and extrapolates. NanoEQL adds chemistry-specific descriptors, smoothed singular operators, structured precursor pooling, process-conditioned gating, and experimental materials validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl
competitive_landscape.difference: PySR searches expression trees with distributed evolutionary optimize-simplify loops and provides a general science benchmark. NanoEQL uses gradient-trained neural symbolic layers and domain-structured branches; it reports higher nanocrystal test R-squared but does not provide a matched search-budget or complexity-frontier comparison.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Learning Models for Colloidal Nanocrystal Synthesis
competitive_landscape.difference: The authors' earlier black-box system trains on 3,500 recipes and predicts size with 1.39 nm MAE plus shape at 89% accuracy, using augmented descriptors and transfer across compositions. NanoEQL reuses that data source but trades some black-box flexibility for sparse equations, explicit precursor gating, and mechanism hypotheses; it does not directly compare on the earlier MAE and shape protocol.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: NanoEQL is the first fully white-box equation-learning architecture for nanocrystal synthesis and offers a general paradigm for chemical mechanism discovery. The original EQL architecture, evolutionary symbolic regression, and the authors' own high-performing nanocrystal predictor all predate it. Reviewer inference: the main novelty is domain engineering—smoothed chemistry-oriented operator functions plus temperature-gated, permutation-invariant precursor pooling that yields three inspectable factors—and the PbSe intervention. Calling the complete network fully white-box is too strong because the reactivity attention scorer remains an MLP and the causal status of the pruned equations is only lightly validated.
reviewer_notes: Performance numbers were checked on pages 5-7, the scalar equation on page 7, gating results on page 10, and the PbSe intervention on pages 11-12. The methods and split protocol were checked on pages 13-17. Competitive titles, identifiers, and scopes were verified on primary arXiv records.
